catalog_quote: Young 2024: "Yami has previously been described ([4], [5]) as exhibiting a default pattern of final-syllable stress for most content words. An exception is found in a smaller lexical class of stative verbs (adjectives), most of which take the prefix ma-, which are reported to show stress on the penultimate syllable instead. Simultaneously, however, stress in Yami is described as contrastive and phonemic, and therefore is claimed to be the sole distinguishing feature between minimal pairs such as matá 'eye' and máta 'raw, uncooked,' although such minimal pairs are rare." Lai & Gooden 2022: "Rau and Dong (2006, p. 82) noted that stress is phonemic in Yami, as in [mapiŋʂán] 'tasty' and [mapíŋʂan] 'organized.' audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the Young 2024 and Lai & Gooden 2022 passages are verbatim in the copies we hold at the stated places. (2) The classification rested second-hand on Rau & Dong 2006 p.82; that monograph is open access at ILAS and was downloaded now: p.82 reads 'Stress is phonemic in Yami.. The default (unmarked) stress is on the ultimate syllable. All other stress has to be marked individually.. The prefix tey- attracts stress', i.e. exactly the description carried by the secondaries, with additional minimal pairs (makapía vs makapiá p.110) and a reduplication stress contrast (p.126). Rau & Dong 2018 sec. 2.3.2 p.19 (downloaded from the CIP online reader) restates it and adds that stative ma- verbs 'mostly' (多半) take penultimate stress and that orthography leaves stress unmarked. sources.quote: p.82: "Stress is phonemic in Yami, e.g., mapingsán 'tasty' vs. mapíngsan 'organized'. The default (unmarked) stress is on the ultimate syllable. All other stress has to be marked individually, e.g., masáray 'happy', masasáray 'every one is happy', mapasózi 'cause to be upset', i'óya 'angry at', mámiying 'laugh', mamiyimíyingen 'love to laugh', and malavlávin 'a cry baby'. The prefix tey- 'most' attracts stress. Stress usually falls on the syllable following tey- 'most' ... sources.quote: "重音雖然大部分落在最後一個音節，但具有辨義功能。為方便讀者學習，凡出現在其他音節者，在音標層次以重音符號（例如：í，á，é，ó）標示。靜態ma-動詞的詞重音多半落在倒數第二音節，例如：masáray「很高興」、masasáray ... mapasózi ... 加上表程度的詞綴tey-「非常、最」，重音也都落在其後的倒數第二音節，例如：teyméhteng「非常溫暖」、teyráhet「非常壞」、teymálma「最懶惰」。但在正式書寫時，為求精簡，重音則不標記。" [Stress mostly falls on the final syllable but is distinctive; non-final stress is marked with an accent in transcription; word stress of stative ma- verbs mostly falls on the penult; with degree prefix tey- stress falls on the following penult; stress is not marked in formal orthography.] Also p.22 rule (5): peripheral vowels in the (unstressed) penult reduce
